title: A fantasy novel universe: 3 kingdoms, 40 characters, 300 years of events
summary: The invented world of the Tidewars saga, organized so a new reader can hold it: three powers, seven eras, and the dozen characters who steer them.

blocks.eyebrow: A reader's map to an invented world
blocks.title: Three powers, one sea, three hundred years
blocks.body: The Tidewars saga spans three centuries and forty named characters, and it does not slow down to explain itself. This is the orientation chapter: the shape of the world, the arc of its history, and the people worth tracking. Everything here is invented - treat it as the saga's front matter.

items.label: Powers: a mountain crown, a river compact, a salt theocracy
Named characters; a dozen actually steer events
Years since the Breaking of the old empire

blocks.title: All of this is made up
blocks.body: Every kingdom, character, date, and proverb on this page was invented for the saga and this reference. Nothing here describes a real place, person, or event - the page's job is to show how a large fictional world can be organized so a reader keeps their footing.

columns.name: Vaelmoor, the Highland Crown
columns.detail: Mountain kingdom of the Vael line. Controls the passes, the mines, and every toll between the rivers and the sea. Proud, old, and permanently convinced it is owed.

columns.name: The Three Rivers Compact
columns.detail: Merchant republic of the river cities Sarre, Lun, and Ild. Rules by ledger rather than crown; its armies are hired, its laws are contracts, and its memory is double-entry.

columns.name: Ashkara, the Salt Coast
columns.detail: Theocracy of the Tide-Speakers, who read divine will in the sea's behavior. Poor in iron, rich in faith, salt, and ships - and the only power whose soldiers believe.

blocks.heading: Vaelmoor: the crown that collects
blocks.body: The Vael kings unified the highlands in the Crown Wars and have taxed everything that moves through their passes since. Their self-image is guardianship - the mountains protect the lowlands from themselves. Everyone else's image is a toll booth with a throne. The current ruler, Queen Idra Vael, is the first of her line to wonder aloud whether the tolls cost more than they earn.

blocks.heading: The Compact: the republic of ledgers
blocks.body: Born in year 96 when the river cities confederated against Vaelmoor tariffs, the Compact is run by consuls elected from the counting houses. Its genius and its rot are the same: everything can be priced, including loyalty. The Three Accountants of Sarre - an office, not a person - quietly hold the debt of half the nobles in the world.

blocks.heading: Ashkara: the coast that listens
blocks.body: The Tide-Speakers began as lighthouse keepers who claimed the sea answered them. Two centuries later their temple is a state. Ashkara's strength is cohesion - a fishing village and a war fleet obey the same tide tables and the same god. Its weakness is succession: when a Tide-Speaker dies, the sea is silent until the priests agree on the next voice, and the sea can stay silent for years.

blocks.heading: Three hundred years in seven eras

items.title: The Splintering
items.detail: The old empire breaks; forty petty kings hold forty valleys. Nothing on the map matches twice in a row.

items.title: The Crown Wars
items.detail: Queen Mabren Vael unifies the highlands by marriage, siege, and one famous avalanche. The Vael line begins.

items.title: The Compact Forms
items.detail: The river cities federate against the crown's tolls. Shipmaster-Consul Yara fen Lunn writes the Articles of the Ledger.

items.title: The Salt Ascension
items.detail: The Tide-Speakers turn a temple into a state. Mera Sol's heresy - that the sea answers everyone, not just priests - is drowned with its author.

items.title: The Ledger Peace
items.detail: Fifty years of trade. The Compact gets rich, the crown gets debt, and Ashkara gets quiet in the way that worries people.

items.title: The War of the Tides
items.detail: Three-power war over the straits. Ends not with a victor but with a storm season that sinks three fleets and everyone's appetite.

items.title: The Concord
items.detail: The present. Queen Idra's fragile union of toll, ledger, and tide - held together, so far, by her refusal to call it permanent.

blocks.quote: The mountains do not pay tolls. They collect them.
blocks.attribution: Vaelmoor proverb, quoted at every negotiating table in the saga

blocks.heading: The dozen who steer (of the forty named)
rows: Unifier of the highlands; everything after her is her shadow
Her grandson; weaponized the passes and provoked the Compact
Wrote the Articles of the Ledger; the republic's founding mind
Lighthouse keeper who heard the sea answer; the faith's origin
Heretic who taught the sea answers everyone; drowned for it, remembered anyway
An office, not a person; holds half the world's debt
Won the straits twice and lost them once, which is why there was a war
King Aelan II, the Winter King
Spent the crown's gold on the war and the passes' goodwill on pride
Ruled during the Silent Years without ever claiming the tide's voice
Sells to all three powers; the saga's recurring question mark
Architect of the Concord; the present tense of the saga
Youngest ever raised to the voice; hears something the priests hoped the sea had forgotten

blocks.heading: How the powers lean on each other

nodes.title: Vaelmoor needs
nodes.detail: Compact grain and loans; Ashkaran salt for the mines.

nodes.title: The Compact needs
nodes.detail: The crown's passes kept open and the temple's ships kept home.

nodes.title: Ashkara needs
nodes.detail: Iron from the highlands and grain from the rivers - and to be believed.

nodes.title: Everyone needs
nodes.detail: The straits calm. The war happened when all three forgot it at once.

blocks.heading: The War of the Tides in four frames

slides.title: The spark (year 221)
slides.body: The Winter King doubles the strait tolls. The Compact's answer is a convoy that simply does not pay, escorted by Brego Dal's fleet.

slides.title: The temple chooses (year 224)
slides.body: Ashkara declares the sea offended by the tolls - theologically convenient, strategically perfect - and closes the straits to everyone.

slides.title: The storm season (year 263)
slides.body: Three fleets sink in one autumn, more to weather than to each other. Every power reads the same omen in its own book.

slides.title: The exhausted peace (year 265)
slides.body: No victor signs the treaty because there is none. The treaty names the sea the straits' only sovereign. Idra Vael, then a princess, watches her father sign and starts planning the Concord.

blocks.heading: Keeping the cast straight while you read

items.label: Track power first, person second
items.detail: Every character acts as their power's interest until the moment they famously do not.

items.label: Vaels come in pairs
items.detail: Each strong Vael ruler is answered by a weak heir; the dynasty breathes in and out.

items.label: When Ashkara goes silent, something is wrong
items.detail: Silence between Tide-Speakers is the saga's omen of choice.

items.label: Leth is never on a side
items.detail: If the spymaster appears loyal, reread the chapter.

blocks.heading: Check your bearings
blocks.prompt: The Three Rivers Compact was founded primarily in response to what?
options: Vaelmoor's tolls on the passes and straits
blocks.explanation: The Articles of the Ledger (year 96) federated the river cities against the Highland Crown's tolls. The empire was fifty years gone by then, and the heresy came later.

blocks.heading: Start with the war, or start with the avalanche
blocks.body: Reading order is a real choice in this saga: publication order opens on the War of the Tides, chronological order opens with Mabren's avalanche. Either way, you now hold the map.
